formation of H2H Innovations, LLC (&#8220;H2H&#8221;), a technology joint venture between
Heartland Resource Technologies (&#8220;Heartland&#8221;) and Hercules.&#160;&#160;The
Dexter transaction included the acquisition of certain inventories for $1.7
million and intangible and goodwill assets of $8.0 million and $1.1 million,
respectively, as well as the assumption of $0.2 million in sales rebate
obligations.&#160;&#160;A total of $10.6 million, including transaction costs of
$0.3 million, was paid during 2007.&#160;&#160;An additional amount of up to
$2.0 million is payable within one year of closing contingent upon the
continuity of sales revenues at certain predetermined levels.&#160;&#160;This
business has been integrated into the Aqualon segment and manufactures and
markets products for the coatings industry.</font></div>

connection with the formation of the H2H joint venture, Hercules made a cash
investment of $5.0 million and contributed certain intangible assets and
royalty-free access to technology for a 51% ownership
interest.&#160;&#160;Heartland contributed similar assets for the remaining 49%
interest.&#160;&#160;As a result of the formation, the Company recognized $13.7
million of intangible assets.&#160;&#160;H2H has been integrated into the
Ventures component of the PTV segment.</font></div>

connection with the 2006 acquisition of the guar and guar derivative
manufacturing division of Benchmark Polymer Products, L.P. (&#8220;Benchmark&#8221;), the
Company is required to make a $2.0 million earn-out payment during 2008 based on
the business&#8217; 2007 performance.&#160;&#160;This contingent payment was accrued
as of December 31, 2007 and charged directly to goodwill.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Also
during 2007, the Company made a $1.4 million earn-out payment that was
previously accrued and charged to goodwill at the end of 2006 based on the
Benchmark business&#8217; 2006 performance.&#160;&#160;In addition, the Company
received a $0.5 million loan repayment from Benchmark Performance Group (&#8220;BPG&#8221;)
in connection with a loan transaction entered into during 2006 (see
below).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2006
Activities</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2006, the Company completed three investment transactions for a total of $29.4
million including transaction costs, net of cash acquired.&#160;&#160;These
included: (1) the acquisition of the Benchmark business, a former subsidiary of
BPG, as well as a loan to BPG that is convertible into an equity position in
BPG, (2) an investment for a 40% ownership interest in the joint venture,
Hercules Tianpu Chemicals Company Limited (&#8220;Hercules Tianpu&#8221;), a manufacturer of
methylcellulose (&#8220;MC&#8221;) in China and (3) the acquisition of the 40% ownership
interest not previously held by Hercules in the joint venture, Shanghai Hercules
Chemicals Company, Ltd. (&#8220;Shanghai Hercules&#8221;), from its partner Shanghai
Chlor-Alkali Chemical Co. Ltd.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company acquired the net assets of Benchmark for a total of $20.2 million
including transaction costs plus a provisional earn-out.&#160;&#160;In addition,
the Company signed a five year exclusive agreement to supply BPG with guar
products for polymer slurries used in oil and gas fracturing
applications.&#160;&#160;Under the terms of the purchase agreement, the Company
acquired Benchmark&#8217;s Dalton, Georgia production facility, related working
capital, an intangible asset of $3.7 million related to the supply agreement and
goodwill of $9.7 million.&#160;&#160;In a related transaction, the Company
loaned $2.5 million to BPG.&#160;&#160;The results of operations of Benchmark
have been included in the Consolidated Financial Statements since the date of
acquisition and have been integrated into the Aqualon segment.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
formation of the Hercules Tianpu joint venture was completed with the Company
contributing a total of $3.2 million for a 40% ownership interest in addition to
$4.4 million previously contributed in 2005 during the preliminary formation
stage.&#160;&#160;Prior to formation, the Company paid a total of $2.8 million
attributable to subscription rights including transaction
costs.&#160;&#160;During 2006, Hercules Tianpu was consolidated into Hercules
(see <a href="#FN3">Note 3</a>) and has been integrated into the Aqualon
business segment.&#160;&#160;Included in the net assets recognized upon
consolidation was $3.5 million of intangible assets as well as $2.8 million of
goodwill.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2006, the Company completed the sale (the &#8220;Transaction&#8221; or &#8220;FiberVisions
Transaction&#8221;) of a 51% interest in its FiberVisions division for $27.0
million.&#160;&#160;In connection with the Transaction, FiberVisions issued
long-term debt in the amount of $90.0 million and simultaneously completed a
distribution of $82.0 million to the Company.&#160;&#160;FiberVisions incurred
$6.3 million of costs in connection with the debt issuance.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Transaction contemplated additional contributions to FiberVisions based on
defined performance measures during 2006 and 2007.&#160;&#160;Based on
FiberVisions&#8217; subsequent performance, the Company provided additional
contributions of $4.5 million and $1.2 million during 2006 and 2007,
respectively.&#160;&#160;As a result of the Transaction and post-closing
adjustments, including the performance-based contributions, the Company
recognized a $13.3 million loss during 2006. During 2007, the Company&#8217;s interest
in FiberVisions was diluted to 34.5% based on additional investments by the
majority owner.&#160;&#160;As a result of the dilution, the Company incurred a
net charge of $2.5 million.&#160;&#160;The 2006 loss and 2007 charge are
included as a component of Other expense, net.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">FiberVisions
was fully consolidated in the Company&#8217;s financial statements through March 31,
2006.&#160;&#160;Effective April 1, 2006, the Company began recording its equity
in the earnings of FiberVisions based on its ownership interest.&#160;&#160;The
Company&#8217;s share of FiberVisions&#8217; net losses for 2007 and 2006 was $1.5 million
and $3.4 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s investment in
FiberVisions is included in Deferred charges and other assets for $18.1 million
as of December 31, 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
connection with its initial commitment to sell a majority interest in
FiberVisions at the end of 2005, the Company recorded an impairment charge of
$52.9 million.&#160;&#160;The impairment charge was based on an estimate of the
fair value for the entire division, as determined by the negotiated sales price
for the aforementioned sale of a majority interest, and was reflected in Profit
from operations as it represented an active and fully consolidated business
during 2005.</font></div>

      holding the option to reset interest rates for one, two, three or six
      month periods.&#160;&#160;The weighted average rate was 6.71% as of
      December 31, 2007.&#160;&#160;The Senior Credit Facility is also comprised
      of a $150 million committed revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Revolving
      Facility&#8221;) which matures on April 8, 2009.&#160;&#160;The Senior Credit
      Facility is secured by liens on the Company's assets (including real,
      personal and intellectual properties) and is guaranteed by substantially
      all of the Company's current and future wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries
      (see <a href="#FN25">Note 25</a>).</font></div>

amounted to $103.6 million and $82.5 million at December&#160;31, 2007 and 2006,

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Of the

increase or decrease within the next twelve months for a number of reasons
including the expiration of statute of limitations, audit settlements, tax
examination activities and the recognition and measurement considerations under
FIN 48.&#160;&#160;The Company does not believe that the total amount of UTB
will significantly increase or decrease over the next twelve
months.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company has a long audit history with the IRS, and recently settled all issues
for the years 1993 through 2003.&#160;&#160;The tax years 2004 and 2005 are
currently under audit by the IRS.&#160;&#160;The Company also files tax returns
in every state which imposes corporate income tax and those jurisdictions remain
subject to examination in accordance with relevant state statutes.&#160;&#160;In
addition, the Company has significant international operations and approximately
50 legal entities have income tax filing requirements in accordance with local
country tax regulations.&#160;&#160;These returns remain subject to examination
in accordance with the local country statutes.&#160;&#160;The Company is
currently under audit in Germany for tax years 1999 through 2004.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company has elected to retain its existing accounting policy with respect to the
treatment of interest and penalties attributable to income taxes in accordance
with FIN 48, and continues to reflect interest and penalties attributable to
income taxes, to the extent they arise, as a component of its income tax
provision or benefit as well as its outstanding income tax assets and
liabilities.&#160;&#160;The total amount of interest and penalties recognized in
the Consolidated Balance Sheet as of January 1, 2007 and December 31, 2007 was
$15.2 million and $16.1 million, respectively.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Description
of Plans</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">U.S.
Defined Benefit Pension Plans</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company provides both funded (qualified) and unfunded (non-qualified)
non-contributory defined benefit pension plans to substantially all of its U.S.
employees.&#160;&#160;During 2004, some terms of the U.S. qualified Plan (&#8220;U.S.
Plan&#8221;) were amended, rendering new hires ineligible and changing the calculation
formula to remaining participants from &#8220;final pay&#8221; to &#8220;modified career average
pay,&#8221; effective January 1, 2005.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">International
Defined Benefit Pension Plans</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company provides defined benefit pension plans to eligible employees in parts of
Europe, the Americas and various countries in the Asia Pacific region (the
&#8220;International Plans&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The International Plans provide benefits
based on years of service and final average salary, except for the defined
benefit pension plans in The Netherlands (&#8220;The Netherlands Plan&#8221;) and the United
Kingdom (the &#8220;U.K. Plan&#8221;) which have both been amended to provide benefits based
on a modified career average pay basis effective January 1, 2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Other
Postretirement Benefit Plans</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
non-pension postretirement benefit plans include group life insurance coverage
and health care reimbursement for eligible employees/retirees in the U.S. and
Canada.&#160;&#160;The benefit obligation of the U.S. postretirement benefit
plan constitutes more than 97% of the Company's consolidated benefit obligation
at December&#160;31, 2007 for non-pension postretirement
benefits.&#160;&#160;The assumed participation rate in these plans for future
eligible retirees was 50% for health care and 100% for life
insurance.&#160;&#160;The health care plans are contributory with participants'
contributions adjusted annually; the life insurance plans are non-contributory
for most retirees.&#160;&#160;The postretirement health care plans include a
limit on the Company's share of costs for recent and future retirees and the
related accounting anticipates future cost-sharing changes to the written plans
that are consistent with the increase in health care
cost.&#160;&#160;Participant contributions are either directly applied to claim
payments or as insurance premiums paid to the insurance companies guaranteeing
the benefits thereunder and thus are not included as contributions to plan
assets.&#160;&#160;U.S. employees hired after December 31, 2002 are ineligible
for retiree life insurance or postretirement health care
benefits.</font></div><br>

initial rate of 10% in 2008 reducing to 5.0% in 2012 and
thereafter.&#160;&#160;The assumed post-65 health care cost trend rate as
of&#160;&#160;December 31, 2007 was an initial rate of 12% in 2009 reducing to
5.0% in 2016 and thereafter.&#160;&#160;A one-percentage point increase in the
assumed health care cost trend rate would increase the postretirement benefit
obligation by approximately $2.3 million and the aggregate service and interest
cost components by $0.1 million, while a decrease of the same magnitude would
decrease the postretirement benefit obligations by approximately $2.3 million
and the aggregate service and interest cost components by $0.2
million.</font></div>

developing an investment strategy for its defined benefit pension plans, the
Company has considered the following factors:&#160;&#160;the nature of the
plans&#8217; liabilities, the allocation of such liabilities between active members
and retired members, the funded status of the plans, the net cash flows of the
plans, the investment horizon of the plans, the size of the plans, historical
and expected capital market returns and the benefits of investment
diversification.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
target asset allocation for the U.S. Plan is 80% long duration fixed income and
20% alternatives.&#160;&#160;&#160;Hercules strategic asset mix for the U.S.
Plan was transitioned in 2007 to decrease exposure to traditional equity market
risks, to utilize asset classes which tend to reduce surplus volatility, and to
utilize asset classes where active management has historically generated
favorable risk-adjusted returns.&#160;&#160;To the extent possible, this asset
mix is intended to substantially mitigate the impact of changes in interest
rates on surplus volatility.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fixed
income securities include U.S. and non-U.S. government obligations and high
grade corporate debt obligations.&#160;&#160;Other investments primarily include
market neutral, long/short, and event driven-type hedge funds plus an allocation
to a global tactical allocation fund.&#160;&#160;Investment managers may employ
limited use of derivatives, including futures contracts, options on futures, and
interest rate swaps in place of direct investment in securities to gain
efficient exposure to markets.&#160;&#160;The expected long-term rate of return
on plan assets was 8.25% for 2007 and 8.50% for 2006.</font></div>

        <div style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Hercules
Incorporated</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes
to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(Dollars
in millions, except per share data)</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Netherlands Plan</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Netherlands Plan's long-term target asset allocation is 40% global equity
securities, 50% fixed income, and 10% alternative investments.&#160;&#160;The
Plan&#8217;s strategic asset mix was transitioned in 2007 to reduce exposure to equity
market risks and to utilize long duration fixed income asset classes levered to
achieve a duration to match the plan&#8217;s liabilities.&#160;&#160;The </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">fixed
income securities are denominated in Euro and are issued and/or guaranteed by
European Monetary Union governments (mainly Belgium, Germany, France, Italy and
The Netherlands).&#160;&#160;The fixed income manager may invest in investment
grade corporate bonds denominated in Euro.&#160;&#160;Investment managers may
employ limited use of derivatives, including futures contracts, options on
futures, and interest rate swaps in place of direct investment in securities to
gain efficient exposure to markets.&#160;&#160;Other investments primarily
include market neutral, long/short, and event driven-type hedge
funds.</font></div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
expected long-term rate of return on plan assets was 6.75% for both 2007 and
2006, respectively.&#160;&#160;The Plan&#8217;s overall expected long-term rate of
return on assets assumption is a function of the target asset allocation for
plan assets, the long-term equilibrium rate of return for the asset class, plus
an incremental return attributable to the active management of plan
assets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">U.K.
Plan</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
target asset allocation for the U.K. Plan is 72% long duration fixed income and
28% of roughly equal proportions of property, hedge, and equity type
investments.&#160;&#160;The U.K.&#8217;s strategic asset mix was transitioned in 2007
to decrease exposure to traditional equity market risks, to utilize asset
classes which tend to reduce surplus volatility, and to utilize asset classes
where active management has historically generated favorable risk adjusted
returns.&#160;&#160;To the extent possible, this asset mix is intended to
substantially mitigate the impact of changes in interest rates on surplus
volatility.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fixed
income securities include both U.K. and non-U.K. Government obligations and high
grade corporate debt obligations.&#160;&#160;Other investments include a market
neutral hedge fund, an international property fund and traditional international
and domestic equity.&#160;&#160;Investment managers may employ limited use of
derivatives, including futures contracts, options on futures, and interest rate
swaps in place of direct investment in securities to gain efficient exposure to
markets.&#160;&#160;The expected long-term rate of return on plan assets was
5.64% and 5.2% for 2007 and 2006, respectively.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Plan
Cash Flows</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Plan
Contributions</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
2007, the Company made contributions to its defined benefit plans totaling $92.1
million, some of which were required by local funding
requirements.&#160;&#160;The Company presently anticipates making voluntary cash
contributions to the U.S. Plan of approximately $22 million during
2008.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the Company anticipates making contributions of
approximately $8 million to its international defined benefit pension plans in
2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company sponsors defined contribution plans or the equivalent thereof in various
jurisdictions in which it operates.&#160;&#160;The most significant of these
plans is the Hercules Incorporated Savings and Investment Plan (the
&#8220;Plan&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Plan is a tax qualified defined contribution 401(k) plan
which covers substantially all U.S. employees.&#160;&#160;Under the Plan, the
Company will contribute an amount equal to 50% of the first 6% of the employees&#8217;
qualified contributions.&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s contributions are made in the
form of Hercules common stock, which vests immediately, contributed through an
Employee Stock Ownership Plan Trust (&#8220;ESOP Trust&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The
Company-contributed common stock may be immediately transferred to other
available investment funds.&#160;&#160;The Company also makes voluntary
contributions to employees&#8217; accounts under the Plan based on the Company&#8217;s
achievement of certain annual financial performance goals.&#160;&#160;Voluntary
contributions can be made in the form of shares from the ESOP Trust, shares from
Reacquired stock and cash at the Company&#8217;s discretion.&#160;&#160;Matching
contributions to the Plan and other voluntary contributions on a combined basis
were $10.7 million, $7.4 million and $5.5 million for 2007, 2006 and 2005,
respectively.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Indemnifications</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
connection with the acquisition, disposition, and purchase or sale of Company
assets and businesses, the Company has indemnified against certain liabilities
that may arise in connection with the relevant transactions and business
activities.&#160;&#160;The terms of these indemnifications typically pertain to
environmental, tax, employee and/or product related matters.&#160;&#160;If the
indemnified party were to incur a liability or have a liability increase as a
result of a successful claim, pursuant to the terms of the indemnification, the
Company would be required to protect, defend, and/or indemnify the
buyer.&#160;&#160;These indemnifications are generally subject to threshold
amounts, specified claim periods and/or other restrictions and
limitations.&#160;&#160;The carrying amount recorded for indemnifications as of
December 31, 2007, all of which are attributable to business disposition
transactions, was $41.2 million and is reflected as a component of Deferred
credits and other liabilities on the Consolidated Balance
Sheet.&#160;&#160;Although it is reasonably possible that future payments may
exceed amounts accrued, due to the nature of indemnified items, it is not
possible to make a reasonable estimate of the maximum potential loss or range of
loss.&#160;&#160;Generally, there are no specific recourse
provisions.</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Hercules
has operating leases (including office space, transportation and data processing
equipment) expiring at various dates.&#160;&#160;Lease expense of $21.0 million,

sub-lease income of $5.1 million, $5.1 million and $5.2 million in 2007, 2006

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At

million in 2011, $11.4 million in 2012 and $10.8 million

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Environmental</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In the
ordinary course of its business, the Company is subject to numerous
environmental laws and regulations covering compliance matters or imposing
liability for the costs of, and damages resulting from, cleaning up sites, past
spills, disposals and other releases of hazardous substances.&#160; Changes in
these laws and regulations may have a material adverse effect on the Company&#8217;s
financial position, results of operations and cash flows.&#160; Any failure by
the Company to adequately comply with such laws and regulations could subject
the Company to significant future liabilities.&#160;&#160;The Company has
established procedures for identifying environmental issues at its plant
sites.&#160; In addition to environmental audit programs, the Company has
environmental coordinators who are familiar with environmental laws and
regulations and act as a resource for identifying environmental
issues.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company has been identified as a potentially responsible party (&#8220;PRP&#8221;) by U.S.
federal and state authorities, or by private parties seeking contribution, for
the cost of environmental investigation and/or cleanup at numerous sites.&#160;
The Company becomes aware of sites in which it may be named a PRP through
correspondence from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;) or other
government agencies or from previously named PRPs, who either request
information or notify the Company of its potential liability.&#160;</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">While the
Company is involved in numerous environmental matters, the following matters are
described below because they are currently viewed by management as potentially
material to the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial position, results of operations
and cash flows.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">United States of America v.
Vertac Chemical Corporation, et al</font>., No. 4:80CV00109 (United States
District Court, Eastern District of Arkansas, Western Division)</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">This
case, a cost-recovery action based upon the Comprehensive Environmental
Response, Compensation and Liability Act (&#8220;CERCLA&#8221; or the &#8220;Superfund statute&#8221;),
as well as other statutes, has been in litigation since 1980, and involves
liability for costs incurred by the EPA in connection with the investigation and
remediation of the Vertac Chemical Corporation (&#8220;Vertac&#8221;) site in Jacksonville,
Arkansas, which was used for the manufacture of certain herbicides and, at the
order of the United States, Agent Orange.&#160;</font></div><br>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
procedural history of this litigation is discussed in greater detail in the
Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2006, and
in other reports subsequently filed by the Company with the U.S. Securities and
Exchange Commission (&#8220;SEC&#8221;).&#160;&#160;In summary, following extended
litigation and appeals, a final judgment against the Company was entered in 2005
by the U.S.&#160;&#160;District Court for the Eastern District of Arkansas, and
upheld in 2006 by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: super">th</font>
Circuit.&#160;&#160;The appellate process ended in 2007 when the U.S. Supreme
Court denied the Company&#8217;s Petition for Certiorari.&#160;&#160;On May 18, 2007,
the Company paid to the United States a total of $124.5 million.&#160;&#160;As a
result, the judgment against the Company has been satisfied, except for such
amounts as may be owed to the United States for additional response costs
incurred since June 1, 1998.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On July
20, 2007, the Company received a claim from the United States seeking
reimbursement of approximately $19 million for response costs incurred since
June 1, 1998, including interest through various points in time preceding May
26, 2007, depending upon the specific cost item claimed.&#160;&#160;The Company
is reviewing these costs to determine whether they are properly
recoverable.&#160;&#160;Should the Company determine that certain costs may not
be properly recoverable, the Company will seek to have the United States&#8217; claim
reduced accordingly.&#160;&#160;In the meantime, as of December 31, 2007, the
Company has accrued $20.0 million, including interest, representing the
Company&#8217;s share of the amount specified by the United States in its claim for
reimbursement.&#160;&#160;The Company will continue to accrue interest on this
amount until payment is made.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Alleghany Ballistics
Laboratory</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 27pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Alleghany Ballistics Laboratory (&#8220;ABL&#8221;) is a government-owned facility which was
operated by the Company from 1945 to 1995 under contract with the United States
Department of the Navy (the &#8220;Navy&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The Navy advised the Company
that, pursuant to CERCLA, it anticipated spending a total of approximately $76
million with respect to certain environmental liabilities which the Navy alleged
were attributable to the Company&#8217;s past operations at ABL.&#160;&#160;Following
negotiations, the Company and the Navy agreed to resolve this matter pursuant to
a Consent Decree for a payment of approximately $13 million, which was approved
by the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Virginia, and which was
paid in December 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Clean Air Act Notice of
Violation</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
December 23, 2005, EPA Region III issued a Notice of Violation (&#8220;NOV&#8221;) to the
Company and to Eastman Chemical Company (&#8220;Eastman&#8221;) alleging various violations
of the Clean Air Act, primarily focused on the Act&#8217;s requirements governing
emissions of volatile organic compounds, at a manufacturing facility located in
West Elizabeth, Pennsylvania. (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">In the Matter of Eastman
Company and Hercules Incorporated</font>, EPA Region III, Docket No.
CAA-III-06-011.)&#160;&#160;That facility was sold to Eastman as part of the
Company's divestiture of its Resins business in May 2001.&#160;&#160;The EPA has
not specifically made a demand for monetary penalties upon the Company and
Eastman.&#160;&#160;The Company is continuing to investigate the allegations set
forth in the NOV, as well as any indemnification obligations that it may owe to
Eastman pursuant to the terms of the purchase and sale agreement.&#160;&#160;At
this time, however, the Company cannot reasonably estimate its liability, if
any, with respect to this matter and, accordingly, has not included this matter
in the accrued liability for environmental matters reported below.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Range of
Exposure</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
reasonably possible share of costs for environmental matters involving current
and former operating sites, including those with identified AROs (see <a href="#FN11">Note 11</a>), the Vertac site, and other locations where the
Company may have a liability, is approximately $98 million as of December 31,
2007.&#160;&#160;These accrued liabilities are evaluated at least quarterly
based on currently available information, including the progress of remedial
investigations at each site and the current status of negotiations with
regulatory authorities regarding the method and extent of apportionment of costs
among other PRPs.&#160;&#160;The actual costs for these matters will depend upon
numerous factors, including the number of parties found responsible at each
environmental site and their ability to pay; the actual methods of remediation
required or agreed to; outcomes of negotiations with regulatory authorities;
outcomes of litigation; changes in environmental laws and regulations;
technological developments; and the remedial activity required, which could last
for an extended number of years.&#160; While it is not feasible to predict the
outcome of all pending environmental matters, the ultimate resolution of one or
more of these environmental matters could have a material adverse effect upon
the Company&#8217;s financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows for
any annual, quarterly or other period.</font></div>

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(Dollars

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Litigation</font></div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
        <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company is involved in litigation arising out of or incidental to the conduct of
its business.&#160; Such litigation typically falls within the following broad
categories:&#160;environmental, including environmental litigation (see above);
antitrust; commercial; intellectual property; labor and employment; personal
injury; property damage; product liability; and toxic tort.&#160;&#160;These
matters typically seek unspecified or large monetary damages or other relief,
and may also seek punitive damages.&#160;&#160;While it is not feasible to
predict the outcome of all pending matters, the ultimate resolution of one or
more of these matters could have a material adverse effect upon the Company&#8217;s
financial position, results of operations and/or cash flows for any annual,
quarterly or other period.&#160;&#160;While the Company is involved in numerous
matters, certain matters are described above and below because they are
currently viewed by management as potentially material.&#160;&#160;From time to
time, management may determine (based on further analysis or additional
information that becomes available through discovery or otherwise) that other
matters are or have become potentially material to the Company.&#160;&#160;As
appropriate, descriptions of such matters will be included in the periodic
report following such determination.&#160;&#160;Occasionally, management may not
determine that a matter is material until it has been settled or otherwise
resolved.&#160;&#160;In such a situation, that matter may not have been
described in the Company&#8217;s periodic reports prior to such settlement or
resolution, but the impact of such settlement or resolution would be reflected
in the financial statements included in the periodic report following such
settlement or resolution.</font></div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Asbestos</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company is a defendant in numerous asbestos-related personal injury lawsuits and
claims which typically arise from alleged exposure to asbestos fibers from resin
encapsulated pipe and tank products which were sold by one of the Company&#8217;s
former subsidiaries to a limited industrial market (&#8220;products claims&#8221;).&#160;
The Company is also a defendant in lawsuits alleging exposure to asbestos at
facilities formerly or presently owned or operated by the Company (&#8220;premises
claims&#8221;).&#160; Claims are received and settled or otherwise resolved on an
on-going basis.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of
December 31, 2007, there were approximately 25,562 unresolved claims, of which
approximately 925 were premises claims and the rest were products claims.&#160;
There were also approximately 1,885 unpaid claims which have been settled or are
subject to the terms of a settlement agreement.&#160;&#160;Between January 1,
2007 and December 31, 2007, the Company received approximately 1,130 new
claims.&#160;&#160;During that same period, the Company spent $24.9 million to
resolve and defend asbestos matters, including $15.8 million directly related to
settlement payments and $9.1 million for defense costs.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As
discussed in greater detail in the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the
year ended December 31, 2006, and in other reports subsequently filed by the
Company with the SEC, in 2002, the Company commenced litigation against its
excess insurance carriers seeking coverage for the Company&#8217;s asbestos-related
liabilities.&#160;&#160;In 2004, that litigation was resolved through several
settlements, resulting in recoveries from some insurers (both cash payments and
monies placed into trust to be used to reimburse the Company for monies spent in
connection with these liabilities), and agreements with other insurers to cover
certain of these liabilities in the future <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">(see
paragraph below)</font>.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2007, all of the cash
recovered and all of the monies placed into trust have been used by the Company
with respect to these liabilities or for other corporate purposes, except for
approximately $24 million remaining in trust and to be paid into trust during
the first quarter of 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">With
respect to the agreements reached to cover these liabilities in the future,
effective October&#160;13, 2004, the Company reached a confidential settlement
agreement with its remaining solvent excess insurers whereby a significant
portion of the costs incurred by the Company with respect to future asbestos
product liability claims will be reimbursed, subject to those claims meeting
certain qualifying criteria (the &#8220;Future Coverage Agreement&#8221;).&#160; That
agreement is not expected to result in reimbursement to the Company, however,
unless and until defense costs and settlement payments for qualifying asbestos
products claims paid by the Company subsequent to the effective date of the
agreement aggregate to approximately $330 million to $370 million, with the
foregoing approximation based on various assumptions, including that there are
sufficient qualifying claims to require such payments, that for such qualifying
claims the time periods of each claimant&#8217;s alleged exposure to asbestos products
falls within the time periods specified in the Future Coverage Agreement, and
that each of the participating insurers remain solvent and honor their
commitments under the terms of the Future Coverage Agreement.&#160; The Company
expects that such amounts, if required to be paid, would be paid by the Company
using monies from the settlements described above and from other sources.&#160;
If and when such amounts are paid by the Company, the insurers&#8217; obligations
pursuant to the terms of the Future Coverage Agreement would be triggered, and
the participating insurers would thereafter be required to pay their allocated
share of defense costs and settlement payments for asbestos product liability
claims that qualify for reimbursement subject to the limits of their liability
pursuant to the terms of the Future Coverage Agreement, which limits are
believed to be sufficient to cover the insurers&#8217; allocated shares of an amount
that exceeds the high end of the reasonably possible range of financial exposure
described below.&#160; The Company will be responsible for the share of such
costs and payments that are not reimbursed by the participating insurers
pursuant to the terms of the Future Coverage Agreement, as well as for such
costs and payments for those claims that do not qualify for reimbursement under
the terms of the Future Coverage Agreement.&#160; Should asbestos reform
legislation be passed, some or all of the obligations under the Future Coverage
Agreement will be suspended for so long as such legislation remains in
effect.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2007, defense costs and settlement
payments for qualifying asbestos products claims of approximately $104 million
have been credited towards the range of $330 million to $370 million noted
above.</font></div><br>

Incorporated</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes
to Consolidated Financial Statements</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(Dollars
in millions, except per share data)</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

      </div>
    </div><br>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
connection with the prior settlements involving payments of cash or the
placement of monies into trust, in general, the Company released the insurers
with which it settled from past, present and future claims under their policies,
agreed to the cancellation of those policies and agreed to indemnify those
insurers from any claims asserted under their policies.&#160;&#160;As a result,
substantial amounts of insurance coverage that would have been available to
cover both asbestos claims and other insured claims have been cancelled and will
no longer be available to cover such claims.&#160;&#160;In connection with the
Future Coverage Agreement, the Company released the participating insurers from
liability under their insurance policies only with respect to asbestos product
liability claims, with the sole liability of those insurers for asbestos product
liability claims being controlled by the Future Coverage Agreement, but with
their insurance policies remaining potentially available to respond to other
insured claims to the extent such policies are triggered, have available limits,
and provide coverage for such claims.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Upon
exhaustion of the monies in trust, which exhaustion is likely to occur during
2008, the Company will be required to fund its asbestos-related liabilities
until the insurers&#8217; obligations under the Future Coverage Agreement are
triggered.&#160;&#160;If and when those obligations are triggered, the Company
and the insurers will share the costs of defending and settling qualifying
asbestos product liability claims, with the amounts paid by the Company versus
the amounts reimbursed pursuant to the Future Coverage Agreement expected to
vary significantly over time, and with the Company typically bearing a larger
share than such participating insurers.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
January 2008, a study commissioned by the Company and prepared by a recognized
expert at a major national university, who is a member of the American Academy
of Actuaries with broad experience in estimating asbestos-related liabilities,
was updated to take into account the then most current data concerning, among
other factors, the Company&#8217;s claims and payment experience.&#160;&#160;As a
result, the Company has decreased the reasonably possible exposure for these
matters as of December&#160;31, 2007 to a range of $255 million to $750 million
(as compared to the prior range of $270 million to $770 million).&#160; Due to
inherent uncertainties in estimating the timing and amounts of future payments,
this range does not include the effects of inflation and has not been discounted
for the time value of money.&#160; In addition, the range of financial exposures
set forth above does not include estimates for future legal costs.&#160;&#160;It
is the Company&#8217;s policy to expense these legal costs as incurred.&#160; Cash
payments related to this exposure are expected to be made over an extended
number of years and actual payments, when made, could be for amounts in excess
of the range due to potential future changes in estimates as well as the effects
of inflation.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
foregoing is based on the Company&#8217;s assumption that the number of future claims
filed per year and claim resolution payments will vary considerably from
year-to-year and by plaintiff, disease, venue and other circumstances, but will,
when taken as a whole, remain relatively consistent with the Company&#8217;s
experience to date and will decline as the population of potential future
claimants expires due to non-asbestos-related causes.&#160; It is also based on
the results of the updated study and the status of the Company&#8217;s settlements
with its insurers, as described above.&#160; However, the Company recognizes
that the number of future claims filed per year and claim resolution payments
could greatly exceed those reflected by its past experience and contemplated by
the study referenced above, that the Company&#8217;s expectations regarding the range
of its reasonably possible financial exposure could change as the study
referenced above is periodically updated, and that its evaluation of the total
payments to be received from its insurers may change depending upon numerous
variables including potential legislation and the risk that one or more
insurance carriers may refuse or be unable to meet their obligations to the
Company.&#160;&#160;Moreover, while the expert noted above has applied his
methodology in determining the Company&#8217;s reasonably possible range of exposures
for these liabilities on a consistent basis, other methods in practice exist
which place a differing degree of emphasis on the underlying variables used to
measure asbestos-related contingencies.&#160;&#160;Such other methods could
yield significantly different ranges of reasonably possible
exposures.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Due to
the dynamic nature of asbestos litigation, the Company&#8217;s estimates are
inherently uncertain, and these matters may present significantly greater
financial exposures than presently anticipated.&#160; In addition, the Company
intends to continue to periodically update the asbestos study referenced above,
and further analysis combined with new data received in the future could result
in a material modification of the range of reasonably possible financial
exposure set forth above.&#160; As a result of all of the foregoing, the
Company&#8217;s liability with respect to asbestos-related matters could vary
significantly from present estimates and may require a material change in the
accrued liability for these matters within the next 12 months.&#160; If the
Company&#8217;s liability does exceed amounts sufficient to trigger the obligations
under the Future Coverage Agreement, the Company presently believes that a
significant portion of the liability it may reasonably anticipate from and after
the date that such obligations are triggered will be reimbursed by monies to be
received pursuant to the Future Coverage Agreement.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
findings of the updated study referenced above identified a range of the
Company&#8217;s reasonably possible financial exposure for these asbestos-related
matters.&#160; The Company adjusted its accrual for present and future potential
asbestos claims before anticipated insurance recoveries at December&#160;31,
2007 to $255.0 million, reflecting the low end of the range noted above in
accordance with GAAP (since no amount within the range is a better estimate than
any other amount).</font></div>

            <td align="left" nowrap valign="bottom" width="1%" style="PADDING-BOTTOM: 4px"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#160;</font></td>

    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
Company, in conjunction with outside advisors, will continue to study its
asbestos-related matters, insurance recovery expectations and reserves on an
ongoing basis, and make adjustments as appropriate.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Composite Products Antitrust
and Qui Tam Matters</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Commencing
in 1999, the Company was one of several companies sued in a series of civil
antitrust and related lawsuits concerning the pricing and sale of carbon fiber
and carbon prepreg products.&#160;&#160;Those products were manufactured and
sold by the Company&#8217;s former Composite Products division, which division was
sold to Hexcel Corporation in 1996.&#160;&#160;As discussed in greater detail in
the Company&#8217;s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2006,
and in other reports subsequently filed by the Company with the SEC, all of
those lawsuits were resolved through settlements.&#160;&#160;It was also
previously reported that the Company had reached a settlement agreement in
principle with two former customers that had opted out of one of those
lawsuits.&#160;&#160;In December 2007, the Company finalized its settlement with
those two former customers and funded that settlement in full.&#160;&#160;As a
result, all of these lawsuits and claims have now been resolved through
settlement.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In May
2007, Cytec Engineered Materials, Inc. filed two lawsuits against the Company
and B.P. Amoco Polymers, Inc. (and allegedly related entities), one in federal
court (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Cytec
Engineered Materials, Inc. v. B.P. Amoco Polymers, Inc., et al</font>., Case No.
SACV 07-528 FMC (RNBx), U.S. District Court, Central District of California,
Western Division), and one in state court (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Cytec
Engineered&#160;&#160;Materials, Inc. v. B.P. Amoco Polymers, Inc., et
al</font>., Case No. BC370895, California Superior Court, Los Angeles
County).&#160;&#160;These lawsuits assert claims against the Company for damages
as a result of some of the anticompetitive activities alleged in the now
resolved lawsuits described in the above paragraph.&#160;&#160;The Company
currently believes that the lawsuits brought by Cytec are without merit and
intends to vigorously defend them.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
December&#160;2004, the Company filed a lawsuit against Hexcel Corporation
(&#8220;Hexcel&#8221;) (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Hercules
Incorporated v. Hexcel Corporation</font>, Supreme Court of the State of New
York, County of New York, Index No.04/604098) seeking indemnification for the
settlements described above.&#160; The lawsuit against Hexcel is based on the
terms of the purchase and sale agreement by which the Company sold its Composite
Products division to Hexcel in 1996.&#160; In response, Hexcel denied liability
and filed a counter-claim also seeking indemnification.&#160;&#160;Both parties
filed motions for summary judgment.&#160;&#160;In April 2007, the trial court
granted Hexcel&#8217;s motion for summary judgment and denied the Company&#8217;s motion for
summary judgment, ruling that the Company is not entitled to indemnification
from Hexcel.&#160;&#160;The Company has appealed those rulings to the Supreme
Court of New York, Appellate Division.&#160;&#160;By Decision and Order dated
February 7, 2008, the Appellate Division affirmed the trial court&#8217;s
rulings.&#160;&#160;The Company is evaluating its options.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Agent Orange
Litigation</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Agent
Orange is a defoliant that was manufactured by several companies, including the
Company, at the direction of the U.S. Government, and used by the U.S.
Government in military operations in both Korea and Vietnam from 1965 to
1970.&#160; In 1984, as part of a class action settlement, the Company and other
defendants settled the claims of persons who were in the U.S., New Zealand and
Australian Armed Forces who alleged injury due to exposure to Agent
Orange.&#160; <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">In Re
&#8220;Agent Orange&#8221; Prod. Liab. Litig.</font>, 597 F. Supp. 740 (E.D.N.Y.
1984).&#160; Following that settlement, all claims for alleged <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">injuries
due to exposure to Agent Orange by persons who had served in the Armed Forces of
those countries were treated as covered by that class action
settlement.</font></font></div>

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Hercules
Incorporated</font></div>
          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(Dollars

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On June
9, 2003, the U.S. Supreme Court affirmed the decision of the U.S. Court of
Appeals for the Second Circuit in a case captioned <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Dow Chemical Company, et al.
v. Daniel Raymond Stephenson, et al.</font>, 123 S. Ct. 2161 (2003), where
plaintiffs Stephenson and Isaacson (in separate but consolidated cases) alleged
that they were injured from exposure to Agent Orange and that such injury did
not manifest until after exhaustion of the settlement fund created through the
1984 class action settlement.&#160; As a result of that decision, the claims of
persons who allege injuries due to exposure to Agent Orange and whose injuries
first manifest themselves after exhaustion of the settlement fund created
through the 1984 class action settlement may no longer be barred by the 1984
class action settlement and such persons may now be able to pursue claims
against the Company and the other former manufacturers of Agent
Orange.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Currently,
the Company is a defendant in approximately thirty-one lawsuits (including two
purported class actions) where plaintiffs allege that exposure to Agent Orange
caused them to sustain various personal injuries.&#160; These alleged exposures
typically occurred while plaintiffs were engaged in activities on behalf of the
military, although one of the lawsuits alleges that civilians who resided near a
military base were exposed as a result of leakage from drums of Agent Orange
that were stored at the base.&#160;&#160;On February&#160;9, 2004, the
U.S.&#160;&#160;District Court for the Eastern District of New York issued a
series of rulings granting several motions filed by defendants in the two cases
that had been remanded to the U.S. District Court by the U.S. Court of Appeals
for the Second Circuit on remand from the U.S. Supreme Court (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">In re: &#8220;Agent Orange&#8221;
Product Liability Litigation: Joe Isaacson, et al v. Dow Chemical Company, et
al. and Daniel Raymond Stephenson, et al. v. Dow Chemical Company, et
al.</font>&#160; (MDL 381, CV 98-6383 (JBW), CV 99-3056 (JBW))).&#160; In
relevant part, those rulings held that plaintiffs&#8217; claims against the defendant
manufacturers of Agent Orange that were brought in the state courts are properly
removable to federal court under the &#8220;federal officer removal statute&#8221; and that
such claims are subject to dismissal by application of the &#8220;government
contractor defense.&#8221;&#160;By Orders dated March&#160;2, 2005, the District Court
dismissed plaintiffs&#8217; claims in all of the lawsuits that were before it at that
time.&#160; Plaintiffs appealed those dismissals to the U.S. Court of Appeals
for the Second Circuit.&#160;&#160;By Opinions dated February 22, 2008, the
Court of Appeals affirmed the rulings of the District Court with respect to the
removal to federal court and the applicability of the &#8220;government contractor
defense&#8221; to those actions brought by persons alleging exposure to Agent Orange
while engaged in activities on behalf of the military, and affirmed the District
Court&#8217;s dismissals of those actions.&#160;&#160;(Joe Isaacson, et al. v. Dow
Chemical Company, et al., Docket No. 05-1820-cv, and additional docket numbers,
and J. Michael Twinam, et. al. v. Dow Chemical Company, et al., Docket No.
05-1760-cv, and additional docket numbers.)&#160;&#160;It is possible that
plaintiffs will seek re-hearing and/or re-hearing <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">en banc</font> by the Court of
Appeals and/or file a Petition for Writ of Certiorari in the United States
Supreme Court.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition, in January&#160;2004, the Company was sued in a purported class action
filed in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York
by The Vietnam Association for Victims of Agent Orange/Dioxin and several
individuals who claim to represent between two and four million Vietnamese who
allege that Agent Orange used by the United States during the Vietnam War caused
them or their families to sustain personal injuries.&#160; (<font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">The Vietnam Association for
Victims of Agent Orange/Dioxin, et al. v. The Dow Chemical Company, et
al.</font>, Civil Action No.&#160;04 CV 0400 (JBW)).&#160; That complaint
alleges violations of international law and war crimes, as well as violations of
the common law for products liability, negligence and international torts.&#160;
The defendants moved to dismiss this case on several grounds, including failure
to state a claim under the Alien Tort Claims Statute, lack of jurisdiction and
justiciability, the bar of the statute of limitations, failure to state claims
for violations of international law, and the &#8220;government contractor
defense.&#8221;&#160; A hearing on these motions was held on February&#160;28,
2005.&#160; By order dated March&#160;10, 2005, the District Court dismissed
this lawsuit.&#160; Plaintiffs appealed that dismissal to the U.S. Court of
Appeals for the Second Circuit.&#160;&#160;By Opinion dated February 22, 2008,
the Court of Appeals affirmed the dismissal of this lawsuit by the District
Court.&#160;&#160;(Vietnamese Association for Victims of Agent Orange, et al. v.
Dow Chemical Company, et al., Docket No. 05-1953-cv.)&#160;&#160;It is possible
that plaintiffs will seek re-hearing and/or re-hearing <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">en banc</font> by the Court of
Appeals and/or file a Petition for Writ of Certiorari in the United States
Supreme Court.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">
      <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition, in 1999, approximately 17,200 Korean veterans of the Vietnam War filed
suit in the 13<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: super">th</font> Civil
Department of the District Court in Seoul, Korea, against The Dow Chemical
Company (&#8220;Dow&#8221;) and Monsanto Company (&#8220;Monsanto&#8221;) for their alleged injuries
from exposure to Agent Orange.&#160;&#160;These lawsuits were filed under
various captions, including <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Dong Jin Kim and 9
others</font>, 99 Gahap 84123, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Il Joo La and 9
others</font>, 99 Gahap 84147, and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Dae Jin Jang</font>, 99
Gahap 84130.&#160;&#160;Following the commencement of those lawsuits, Dow and
Monsanto petitioned the court to issue Notices of Pendency to each of the
non-defendant manufacturers of Agent Orange, including the Company, in an
attempt to bind those companies to factual and legal findings which may be made
in the Korean courts if Dow and Monsanto are held liable to plaintiffs and sue
those companies for contribution.&#160;&#160;Thereafter, the Company was served
with such notices through diplomatic channels.&#160;&#160;In 2002, the District
Court dismissed the plaintiffs' claims, and the plaintiffs
appealed.&#160;&#160;It has been reported that on January 26, 2006, the
intermediate appellate court in Seoul reversed the District Court and awarded
damages of $65.2 million plus pre- and post-judgment interest to approximately
6,800 of the approximately 17,200 plaintiffs that filed these
lawsuits.&#160;&#160;The Company has been informed that Dow and Monsanto have
appealed.&#160;&#160;If Dow and Monsanto are not successful on appeal, it is
possible that they might initiate an action seeking contribution from the
non-defendant manufacturers of Agent Orange, including the
Company.&#160;&#160;Further, if the intermediate appellate court&#8217;s decision is
ultimately upheld, it is possible that new lawsuits could be brought in Korea
against the Agent Orange manufacturers, including the Company, by other Korean
veterans of the Vietnam War.</font></div>

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Notes

          <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">(Dollars
